gen-dafont-disorder-gf-sulphur-point: Disorder scatters its glyphs wide apart and looks gleefully rough. Sulphur Point's plain sans build, marker-like in weight and bulky in the lowercase, gives all that mess something solid to stand on.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-tiktok-sans: Disorder is raw and chaotic, with no hairline anywhere in sight. TikTok Sans, plain sans with lowercase climbing nearly to cap height, tames the wildness above it into something orderly.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-ubuntu-sans: Chaotic and raw, Disorder spaces its big-looking lowercase well apart on the line. And Ubuntu Sans brings sans-serif tubular strokes, like bent copper pipe, with lowercase eyes big as washers.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-vend-sans: Disorder's oversized-looking lowercase, spaced well apart and with no swelling where curves meet stems, gives it a raw, chaotic edge. Vend Sans, a ruler-drawn sans, matches that size without the mess.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-yaldevi: Yaldevi is a sans-serif with outsized lowercase and an e whose eye opens clearly to the right. And beneath Disorder's ruler-straight rowdy headings, paragraphs of it would move along smoothly and cleanly.
gen-dafont-dited-fs-gambetta: Gambetta feels bookish and graceful, though it isn't made for lengthy paragraphs. Dited packs its round letters hip to hip with wide openings for a digital snap, while Gambetta's gentle stroke taper does the soft, refined work.
gen-dafont-dited-fs-neco: Neco reads dignified and authoritative, most at home in modest helpings. Its swell from hairline to stem stays measured and never pinches, while Dited's digital shapes sit hip to hip above it.
gen-dafont-dited-fs-recia: Dited sits its shapes hip to hip on the line, with wide, inviting openings on every round letter. Dited shouts; Recia, a serif, stays sharp but wants a little text.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-aldrich: Aldrich has round, cupped letters drawn as if with a round-tipped pen. Dogica's wide tracking and open curve ends lead, while their shared near-capital lowercase makes the two feel like kin.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-alexandria: Alexandria leaves generous gaps at its c terminals, with short stems above and below a tall body. And in running text Alexandria would read cleanly and steadily, a calm counterweight to Dogica's heavy width.
